candidates.source_name: ČNB – Obecný přístup ke stanovení minimálního požadavku na kapitál a způsobilé závazky (MREL) a sekce Řešení krize
candidates.why_relevant: ČNB as resolution authority publishes its general methodology for setting MREL — 2*(P1+P2) for large/systemically important/complex banks earmarked for bail-in, and (P1+P2) + coefficient*(P1+P2) for mid-sized, less complex banks resolved via transfer to a private acquirer — plus transition periods and an aggregate estimate that banks would need to add roughly CZK 120–140bn. ČNB explicitly does not publish bank-by-bank MREL values, so this methodology page is the only public way to reverse-engineer why and when a given Czech bank must come to market with senior non-preferred or subordinated paper. It is the demand driver behind most non-covered bank issuance in this cell.

candidates.why_relevant: Commercial bond-market database with per-issuer and per-ISIN pages for Czech bank paper, carrying identifiers (ISIN, FIGI, WKN), coupon, maturity, currency and rating history. Retrieved examples for Česká spořitelna alone span EUR, USD and perpetual CZK instruments (XS2676413235, XS2555412001, XS2638560156, XS2746647036, XS2852933329, XS2930541698, AT0000A2STV4, CZ0003704769) — an inventory that is far quicker to assemble here than by walking every issuer site. The AT-prefixed identifier is a useful hint that some ČS paper is issued/listed via Austrian infrastructure.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Use as a cross-check/enrichment layer only, at low volume and within the site's terms; prefer the official ČNB registers and issuer pages as the system of record. A paid API/subscription would be needed for systematic extraction.
candidates.discovered_via_method: en searches on Czech bank EUR bonds; recurring aggregator across multiple result sets
queries_used: Erste Group debt investor relations covered bonds Ceska sporitelna cover pool data
Wiener Borse listed Czech bank covered bond Ceska sporitelna Vienna Stock Exchange bond listing prospectus

candidates.source_name: Hypoindex.cz – tiskové zprávy / rubrika emise hypotečních zástavních listů
candidates.why_relevant: Czech mortgage-market trade portal that reprints bank press releases about HZL issues, often with volume, coupon and target investor group, and provides a running commentary on which banks are leaning on covered-bond funding in a given month. Useful as a low-cost early-warning feed and as an archive of older HZL issues (multiple Česká spořitelna HZL announcements of CZK 2bn/4bn/5bn were surfaced this way) that the banks themselves have since removed from their sites.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: RSS/section polling weekly with keyword filter on 'hypoteční zástavní listy', 'emise', 'kryté dluhopisy'; use only as a discovery trigger, then verify against the ČNB final-terms register or the issuer page.
candidates.discovered_via_method: cs seed query on hypoteční zástavní listy; recurring domain across several cs result sets
queries_used: hypoteční zástavní listy emise prospekt banka Česká republika
"Česká spořitelna" hypoteční zástavní listy "základní prospekt" emisní dodatek csas.cz povinně uveřejňované informace

candidates.source_name: J&T Banka a Fio banka – komentáře k emisím MREL dluhopisů (broker research notes / zprávy z burzy)
candidates.why_relevant: Czech brokers publish short, dated notes on each domestic MREL/SNP issue, frequently ahead of or alongside the formal filing, and give pricing colour that issuers omit. Retrieved examples cover Banka CREDITAS MREL issues at 7.5% and MONETA's MREL programme — including a CZK 1.5bn issue at an 8% coupon, a mandate for a EUR 300m six-year non-call-five MREL bond at 4.41% p.a., nine-times oversubscription, bookrunners BNP Paribas and JPMorgan with Goldman Sachs Bank Europe and J&T Banka as co-managers, and the resulting +453bp move in MREL ratio to 28.23% against a 22.45% management target. That level of transaction detail is not in any prospectus.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Poll the article feeds of jtbank.cz, fio.cz/zpravodajstvi and zpravy.kurzy.cz weekly with a keyword filter on 'MREL', 'emise dluhopisů', 'kryté dluhopisy', 'podřízené dluhopisy'; extract issuer, size, coupon, structure, bookrunners.
candidates.discovered_via_method: cs searches on MREL bond issuance; recurring broker-commentary cluster
queries_used: Komerční banka emise dluhopisů MREL nepodřízené dluhopisy senior non-preferred tisková zpráva
MONETA Money Bank covered bonds kryté dluhopisy MREL bond issuance investor relations debt
Banka CREDITAS MREL dluhopisy prospekt emise investoři kryté dluhopisy

candidates.source_name: Fitch Ratings – Czech covered bond rating actions (e.g. Komerční banka soft bullet covered bonds)
candidates.why_relevant: Rating agency covered-bond commentary carries the analytics behind a programme — OC levels relied upon, D-Cap/discontinuity assessment, cover-pool credit assumptions, refinancing spreads — that neither the prospectus nor the HTT states as a judgement. KB's programme is rated AAA (Stable) by Fitch as of 24 June 2026; Česká spořitelna's inaugural covered bond was Moody's Aaa. Rating actions are also the most reliable public signal that a programme has changed materially.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Subscribe to Fitch/Moody's/S&P rating-action alerts filtered to Czech Republic + covered bonds/banks; capture headline, date, rating and rationale summary. Full reports generally require a login — treat headlines and press releases as the collectable layer.
candidates.discovered_via_method: snowballed from the Komerční banka EUR covered bond investor page, which links the rating action directly
queries_used: Komerční banka "pro investory" dluhopisy debt investors covered bond programme EUR 5 bn

negative_findings.description: Searched in Czech for a national aggregator of covered-bond investor reports / cover-pool data (terms: 'kryté dluhopisy', 'krytý blok', 'evidence krytých bloků', 'seznam emitentů', ČNB Vyhláška č. 2/2019 Sb. o evidenci krytých bloků). ČNB maintains the register of permitted covered blocks and labelled ISINs, and issuers must regularly report to ČNB on compliance, but no public Czech portal publishes the underlying cover-pool data.
negative_findings.result_summary: No national HTT/cover-pool portal exists for CZ. Cover-pool disclosure is issuer-by-issuer (KB, UniCredit CZ&SK, MONETA, Česká spořitelna) plus the pan-European Covered Bond Label. The ČNB register gives issuer names, LEI/IČO and ISINs only — no pool composition, LTV, OC or arrears data.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection for this cell cannot be centralised on one regulator feed. The pipeline must fan out to six issuer sites (some bot-defended) and to coveredbondlabel.com, and must treat the ČNB list as the completeness check rather than the data source.

negative_findings.description: Plain HTTP fetches to several Czech bank disclosure hosts were refused: unicreditbank.cz returned HTTP 403 on both /cs/o-bance/dluhopisy-prehled.html and /en/ostatni/debt-investor-relations.html; creditas.cz returned 403 on /o-bance/pro-investory; csob.cz returned HTTP 500 on /csob/povinne-uverejnovane-informace; csobhypotecni.cz returned HTTP 500 on /o-bance/emise-hzl and /o-bance/zpravy-o-hospodareni-dokumenty/.
negative_findings.result_summary: Four issuer hosts are unreadable by simple fetch, yet PDF documents on the very same hosts are indexed and referenced from search results, which strongly suggests bot defence / edge-WAF behaviour rather than dead pages.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: This is a hypothesis, not a verdict — none of these should be recorded as dead. The collector for this cell needs a headless-browser tier with realistic headers for HTML index pages, while direct GET on /content/dam/, /documents/ and /files/ PDF paths appears sufficient for the documents themselves.

negative_findings.description: coveredbondlabel.com issuer pages and the issuer directory were fetched statically. The Komerční banka issuer page (id 177) rendered its contact list, pool programme list, bond list and HTT section all as '0-10 of 0', and /issuers/directory rendered an empty filter table. /issuers and /national-information both returned HTTP 404.
negative_findings.result_summary: The Label's Czech data exists but is client-side rendered; static scraping yields empty tables and would falsely suggest Czech issuers publish nothing.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A naive collector would record the three labelled Czech issuers as having no HTT filings. Headless rendering is mandatory here, and the correct paths are /issuers/directory, /issuers/national/list, /new-htt and /htt-database.

negative_findings.description: Raiffeisenbank a.s. (covered blocks RBCZ_BLOCK_02 and RBCZ_BLOCK_03, with labelled issue XS3019003253) and Hypoteční banka (HB-Blok 4) both appear in the ČNB covered-block register, but Czech- and English-language searching surfaced no dedicated public cover-pool/HTT/investor-report page for either. RBCZ's securities page references an 'International Covered Bonds Programme' without a linked cover-pool report; Hypoteční banka's trail is prospectus/emisní-dodatek only. Neither was found among Covered Bond Label issuers (KB, UniCredit CZ&SK and Česká spořitelna were the three identified).
negative_findings.result_summary: Two of six licensed Czech covered-block issuers have no located public cover-pool disclosure surface.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Cover-pool coverage for CZ is structurally incomplete: any CZ-wide covered-bond comparison built from public sources will be missing Raiffeisenbank and Hypoteční banka, which must be flagged rather than silently treated as zero.

negative_findings.description: No settled Czech-language term for 'senior non-preferred' was found in issuer or regulator material. Czech sources use descriptive constructions — 'nepodřízené dluhopisy', 'podřízené dluhopisy', 'MREL dluhopisy', 'způsobilé závazky' — and Raiffeisenbank's own documents use the English 'SNP (Senior Non Preferred)' inside Czech text. Similarly, 'covered bond' has three coexisting Czech renderings depending on vintage and legal basis: the historic 'hypoteční zástavní listy (HZL)', the post-2019 statutory 'kryté dluhopisy' / 'krytý blok', and the EU-label 'evropský krytý dluhopis (prémiový)'.
negative_findings.result_summary: Local-language querying works, but only with an explicitly multi-vintage term set; a single-term query misses whole eras of documents.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Any CZ query set for this cell must fire all of {hypoteční zástavní listy, HZL, kryté dluhopisy, krytý blok, evropský krytý dluhopis, emisní dodatek, konečné podmínky, základní prospekt, MREL dluhopisy, způsobilé závazky} plus the English-in-Czech forms (SNP, MREL, HTT, cover pool), or recall collapses.

negative_findings.description: The Czech terms 'dluhopisy' and 'emise dluhopisů' are heavily contaminated by the Czech retail corporate-bond and mini-bond scene (dluhopisy.cz, dluhopisar.cz, srovnavacdluhopisu.cz, KB's large archive of arranged client issues for Accolade, Allwyn, CZG, Dr. Max, RegioJet and others) and by bank product pages selling third-party bonds. Searching 'banka emise dluhopisů' without qualifiers returns mostly non-bank issuers for whom the bank is merely arranger or paying agent.
negative_findings.result_summary: Broad Czech bond queries have low precision for bank-as-issuer material.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Query design must anchor on issuer-role terms ('emitent', 'povinně uveřejňované informace', 'krytý blok', 'MREL') or on the named six licensed issuers; otherwise the collector fills up with corporate mini-bond noise that belongs to a different cell entirely.

negative_findings.description: The session's WebSearch budget (200/200) was consumed before three planned lines of enquiry could be run: (a) the Czech-language route into the ČNB OAM application interface and its filter vocabulary, (b) ČNB ARAD time series for HZL/covered-bond outstanding volumes, and (c) MREL/bond issuance by second-tier Czech deposit-takers and building societies (Air Bank / PPF banka, J&T Banka, Fio banka, Českomoravská stavební spořitelna, Modrá pyramida, Trinity Bank).
negative_findings.result_summary: Three known-relevant sub-areas were left unsearched; they are recorded as coverage gaps rather than as absent sources.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Absence of these from the candidate list reflects a run constraint, not a finding that the sources do not exist. They should be the first queries in any follow-up run for this cell.

coverage_gaps.description: Most Czech bank EUR covered bonds and MREL paper carry XS identifiers, and Česká spořitelna's inaugural covered bond is listed on the Vienna Stock Exchange regulated market (with at least one AT-prefixed ČS instrument observed, AT0000A2STV4). The disclosure pages of the foreign listing venues — Wiener Börse, and the Luxembourg / Euronext Dublin venues typically used for XS paper — were not enumerated in this run.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a dedicated pass over Wiener Börse, Luxembourg Stock Exchange and Euronext Dublin issuer/security pages for the six licensed Czech covered-block issuers plus MONETA and Raiffeisenbank, keyed on the ISINs already extracted from the ČNB register; these venues host prospectus repositories and ongoing-disclosure notices that mirror or supplement issuer sites.

coverage_gaps.description: Only the six ČNB-licensed covered-block issuers plus Banka CREDITAS were mapped. Other Czech deposit-takers with MREL obligations and likely bond issuance — Air Bank / PPF banka, J&T Banka, Fio banka, Trinity Bank, Max banka — and the building societies (Českomoravská stavební spořitelna, Modrá pyramida, Raiffeisen stavební spořitelna) were not systematically searched. PPF banka already surfaced as a prospectus host in one result set.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Query each institution in Czech with the pattern '<banka> povinně uveřejňované informace dluhopisy emise prospekt' and '<banka> MREL dluhopisy emise', and independently sweep the ČNB final-terms register filtered to credit-institution issuers to catch any bank missed by name-based searching.

coverage_gaps.description: No aggregate time series of Czech covered-bond / HZL outstanding volumes was located. ČNB ARAD is the obvious candidate database but was not reached before the search budget ran out; the CDCP Fact Book and the ECBC Fact Book Czech chapter are partial substitutes.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Search ČNB ARAD in Czech for 'hypoteční zástavní listy' and 'kryté dluhopisy' series, and check the ČNB financial-market statistics section, so issuer-level cover-pool data can be normalised against a market total.

coverage_gaps.description: Both ČNB registers that matter most here — the prospectus register and the final-terms register — are served by a legacy Oracle PL/SQL web application (oam.cnb.cz/sipresextdad/SIPRESWEB...) with form-driven input and no observed API, JSON endpoint, RSS or bulk export. The covered-block issuer list is a hand-maintained PDF.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build a resilient scraper with a headless-browser fallback and a stable ISIN/LEI/IČO join key; hash the covered-block PDF for change detection. Also test whether ESMA's EU-level prospectus register mirrors ČNB approvals, which would give a cleaner feed for the same content.

coverage_gaps.description: Moody's and S&P covered-bond analytics for Czech programmes (ČS's inaugural bond is Moody's Aaa; KB is Fitch AAA) sit largely behind registration or subscription. Only the Fitch rating-action headline linked from KB's own investor page was reachable in this run.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Register for free agency accounts to obtain rating-action press releases and performance-overview summaries, and treat issuer-page rating links (as on KB's covered bond page) as the reliable free entry point. Do not plan on systematic extraction of full agency reports.

coverage_gaps.description: Transaction announcements from deal counsel and arrangers (A&O Shearman on both the ČS EUR 500m inaugural covered bond and a UniCredit CZ&SK EUR 500m mortgage covered bond issuance; bookrunner line-ups disclosed via broker notes) proved to be a fast, well-dated channel that often describes programme structure before the issuer publishes anything. Only incidental examples were captured.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a standing sweep of the Czech capital-markets practice news feeds (A&O Shearman, Clifford Chance, White & Case, Kinstellar, PRK Partners, Allen Overy CZ) and of the British Chamber of Commerce CZ and Czech Banking Association news pages, filtered on 'covered bond', 'krytý dluhopis', 'MREL', to catch deal announcements at T+0.

brief: The Czech debt-investor disclosure channel has an unusually clean spine: ČNB publishes the closed list of six banks licensed to run a covered block (UniCredit Bank CZ&SK, Česká spořitelna, Hypoteční banka, MONETA Money Bank, Raiffeisenbank and Komerční banka) with LEI/IČO and the ISINs entitled to the 'European Covered Bond (Premium)' label, and runs two Oracle-based registers — approved prospectuses and final terms/emisní dodatky — that together date-stamp essentially every bank bond programme and tranche in the country, plus an OAM store that captures regulated filings from debt-only issuers invisible to equity IR. The rich data, though, lives on the issuer side and is uneven: Komerční banka and MONETA publish exemplary debt pages (quarterly Covered Bond Investor Reports, machine-readable HTT workbooks, cover-pool overviews, full AT1/T2/SNP prospectus stacks), Česká spořitelna began HTT reporting in 2026 on a CZK 308.5bn cover pool, UniCredit CZ&SK runs the largest labelled XS franchise behind a 403-guarded site, while Raiffeisenbank and Hypoteční banka hold licensed cover pools with no cover-pool disclosure surface located at all. Terminology is the main recall risk — three coexisting Czech renderings (hypoteční zástavní listy, kryté dluhopisy/krytý blok, evropský krytý dluhopis) and no native term for senior non-preferred — and four issuer hosts (UniCredit, ČSOB, ČSOB Hypoteční banka, CREDITAS) returned 403/500 to plain fetches while their PDFs remain reachable, so a headless-browser tier is a prerequisite rather than an optimisation. Pan-European scaffolding (Covered Bond Label HTT database, ECBC Fact Book, free NORD/LB Floor Research) fills the interpretive layer and is the fastest way to detect a new Czech filing.
